text:
tara_support: FYI — Acme ingestion reported intermittent 429 bursts for POST /v1/batch/embeddings over the last ~2h. They attached a HAR but no request IDs in responses. Asking for steps we can give them to reproduce with curl + exact headers so we can correlate logs.

sam_eng: Can you ask them for the full response headers (all X- and Ratelimit headers) and any 'X-Request-ID' or 'Request-Id' values? Without those we can't tie to proxy logs. Also request a minimal curl that reproduces (single-threaded first).

tara_support: Sending suggested repro curl to customer now:

```bash
# basic single-request repro (include -v to capture headers)
curl -v \
  -X POST 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/batch/embeddings' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: my-test-<uuid>' \
  --data '{"input": ["text1","text2"]}' \
  --compressed
```

Please ask them to run that and paste the whole curl stdout/stderr (including response headers). If they see 429 include the exact response headers and body.

mohit_sre: Also ask them to run with --trace-time and capture timing, e.g.:

```bash
curl -v --trace-time --trace-ascii /tmp/curl.trace -H 'X-Request-ID: <uuid>' ...
```

We specifically need these headers if present: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, `Retry-After`, and any `X-Redwood-Request-ID` or `Request-ID`. If their client strips headers or hides them, tell them to run `curl -i` (include headers) and attach output.

infra-bot: deploy-monitor: observed short-lived spike of rate-limiter triggers across eu-central around 2026-03-03T14:20:45Z — correlating logs may help once we have request ids.

ben_support: If they're on Dedicated, remind them reserved throughput might be hit if they send concurrent producers. If on Hosted, suggest backoff w/ exponential jitter and honoring `Retry-After`. But first we need correlation ids.

sam_eng: If curl doesn't reproduce, ask them to run a tiny concurrency test so we can observe burst behaviour:

```python
# small test using requests, concurrency=4
import requests, uuid, threading
url = 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/batch/embeddings'
headers = {'Authorization':'Bearer <REDACTED>','Content-Type':'application/json'}
body = {'input':["x"]}

def post():
    headers['X-Request-ID'] = 'repro-' + str(uuid.uuid4())
    r = requests.post(url, json=body, headers=headers, timeout=30)
    print(r.status_code, r.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Remaining'), r.headers.get('Retry-After'), headers['X-Request-ID'])

threads = [threading.Thread(target=post) for _ in range(4)]
for t in threads: t.start()
for t in threads: t.join()
```

That will give them per-request request ids and headers we can use.

tara_support: I'll ask them to: 1) run the single curl with -v, 2) attach the raw trace / curl output if 429 happens, 3) run the small python concurrency test and paste stdout, and 4) include the tenant/project id + time window (UTC) for when failures happened. Also ask them to send the top 20 `X-Request-ID` values from their side.

mohit_sre: Once we have request ids I'll pull the proxy and rate-limiter logs and check batching and token accounting windows — looking for boundary effects where many small concurrent requests bypass batching and hit per-request limit bursts. If we see it, we can propose an immediate mitigation (short client-side cold-start delay or small client-side queue).

tara_support: I'll message the customer now. If they give us the HAR, ask them to export the HAR with full headers (DevTools -> preserve log -> export HAR) and not to redact the Request-Ids.

ben_support: Also ask billing/accounting for their plan name — if they believe quota mismatch we should confirm quota config.

tara_support: Thanks team :thumbsup: I told them to include all outputs in one reply and I'll paste here when they send it.
